pipeline.signal_source: Existence: residual flat-region noise p50 (residual = target - clean, clean-gradient<8 mask) target 69.4/160.4/100.0/53.8/49.0 on pairs 0-4; matched deterministic backbone (blur3+jpeg4) leaves this unexplained. Subtype: chroma std — YCrCb3 sim Cb overshoots +55.8% on pair0 (5.77 vs target 3.71) while target Cb equals the JPEG-only level (R0 q8 calibration 3.73); over 5 pairs mean |dCb| YCrCb3 20.7% (max 55.8%) vs RGB4 6.0% (max 18.4%), mean |dCr| 6.9% vs 4.9%. Mechanism: noise_gaussian_YCrCb sev3 has sigma_chroma=1.9x sigma_luma (x_distortion/noise.py), mechanically producing chroma excess absent in the target; RGB noise has effective chroma ~0.62x luma. Severity: flat-region residual p50 ratios sim/target for RGB4 = 0.71/1.05/1.00/1.00/0.66 (exact on pairs 2/3); RGB3 is 0.27x-0.75x (far too weak, e.g. 18.8 vs 69.4 pair0); YCrCb4 overshoots 2.0x on pair0 and wrecks chroma (Cb +95%). Global second-order fit: RGB4 variance_ratio |err| mean 3.9% (max 6.8%), mean_shift |err| mean 0.75 levels (max 1.28) -> no global step required, consistent with R1's removal of contrast. Judged by verify_signals + second-order statistics; PSNR not used (noise seed mismatch). Verdict stays UNCERTAIN (SKILL: noise steps never LIKELY; noise->blur subtype is Tier C, 54.7%).

Blur presence certain: spectral_slope_ratio 1.20-1.28 and gm_ratio 0.17-0.50 in 5/5 (fresh R2 run_full_analysis). Severity nailed by the noise-robust checks: with the R2 candidate, blur:spectral_slope matched in 5/5 (pair0 target -1.1488 vs sim -1.1633, diff 0.0145 < 0.08) and wiener_kernel corr 0.9994 (>0.85; matched 5/5). R2 severity scan falsifies neighbours: blur_gaussian:2 -> slope diff 0.148 (fail), blur_gaussian:4 -> slope diff 0.171 (fail), while sev3 diff 0.0145. Not motion: residual_anisotropy 1.41/1.15/1.35/1.65/1.67 < 1.7 (pairs 3/4 borderline but below). Glass_score 1.15-1.54 lies inside the no-blur JPEG sim range 1.44-1.86 -> GLASS verdict is a JPEG-confounded FP. gaussian vs lens MTF-indistinguishable; gaussian retained.

block_boundary 7.15/4.24/5.79/4.81/6.08 (>>1.05, 0% FP signal) and dct_zero_ratio 0.892-0.948 in 5/5 (fresh R2 run_full_analysis reproduces R1 exactly). Severity 4 retained: fresh R2 baselines reproduce R1's cross-pair split (bb diff 13%/24%/25%/match/match for jpeg4), and jpeg5 was already rejected in R1 (pair0 bb diff 40% vs 10-13% for jpeg4, worse chroma). With the R2 noise candidate (RGB4) the bb agreement improves (diff 11%/16%/match/match/match; dct zero_ratio diff 0.005-0.019) -> jpeg4 remains the best cross-pair compromise. Severity borders sev5 on pairs 1/2 but sev+-1 JPEG costs ~0.2 dB (REFLECTION_MECHANISM).

change_vs_R1.only_change: noise function + severity (YCrCb:3 -> RGB:4); blur and JPEG steps unchanged
change_vs_R1.basis: Second-order statistics on 5 matched support pairs: mean |dCb| 20.7% -> 6.0% (max 55.8% -> 18.4%), mean |dCr| 6.9% -> 4.9%, mean_shift |err| 1.15 -> 0.75 levels, flat-residual ratio error 25.9% -> 13.8%; var_ratio mean |err| 3.3% -> 3.9% (only metric slightly worse; max improves 8.6% -> 6.8%). verify_signals verdict count improves: YCrCb3 2 PARTIAL/3 WEAK -> RGB4 3 PARTIAL/2 WEAK.

removed_steps.signal_source: R2 fresh run_full_analysis still returns inconsistent per-pair global verdicts for the SAME pipeline (NO_GLOBAL / CONTRAST_weaken_sev4 / NO_GLOBAL / CONTRAST_weaken_sev3 / SATURATION_weaken_sev4, all low confidence) -> coupling artifact, not a real global step. The R2 noise candidate reproduces variance_ratio (mean |err| 3.9%) and mean_shift signs/magnitudes (mean |err| 0.75 levels) on all 5 pairs without any global function. Library contrast_weaken_scale sev1 (alpha=0.75) overshoots (var_ratio 0.42-0.44 in R1 tests) and is not representable closer to the implied alpha>=0.96. No global step added.

alternatives.stats: R1 primary. Second-order on 5 pairs (same basis): mean |dCr| 6.9% (max 14.1), mean |dCb| 20.7% (max 55.8), var_ratio |err| mean 3.3% (max 8.6), mean_shift |err| 1.15 levels, flat-residual ratio err mean 25.9%. R1-trained model reached support PSNR 23.63 (R0 20.56).
alternatives.reason: Fallback if the chroma-statistics reading is wrong; carries the only trained-model evidence so far (R1 ckpt 23.63 support). Better global var_ratio (3.3% vs 3.9%) but far worse chroma (Cb 20.7% vs 6.0%) and flat-noise fit.

alternatives.stats: Same-family lower severity. Chroma good (mean |dCr| 4.4%, |dCb| 5.5%) but flat-region residual noise 3-4x under target (pair0 18.8 vs 69.4; pair2 75.1 vs 100.0) and var_ratio overshoots (+14.3% pair0).
alternatives.reason: Second-best noise candidate; use only if RGB4 proves too strong in training (support PSNR drop).
